top.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
top.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings Verstappen in control despite lead changes "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. top.title: Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings
top.description: Max Verstappen said George Russell's lock-up was "karma" for his comments about the Dutchman earlier in the Las Vegas weekend [Getty Images] Max Verstappen sealed his fourth win of the season with a stunning victory at a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver fought off his rivals for the lead throughout the race and crossed the line ahead of the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. George Russell, who started second, locked up late on attempting a move on Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and finished ninth, while Charles Leclerc was given a 10-second time penalty for making contact with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Vegas. Max Verstappen - 10/10 An extraordinary display of racecraft. Inherited pole after Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty and spent virtually the entire race being attacked, passed and then finding a way back through, while also working out the optimum energy deployment from inside his Red Bull. One of his finest victories. Lando Norris - 9/10 A remarkable recovery after dropping as low as 11th in the madness of the opening part of the race. Had genuine pace throughout and fought all the way back to second, finishing less than a second behind Verstappen. Oscar Piastri - 9.5/10 One of the drives of the race. Qualified seventh but started 17th because of his engine penalty and charged all the way through to the podium, gaining 14 places and joining McLaren team-mate Norris in passing Antonelli right at the end. Kimi Antonelli - 9.5/10 Fastest of everyone in qualifying and a genuine contender for victory despite starting sixth because of his engine penalty. Battled Verstappen superbly before his Mercedes' energy deployment problem on the final lap cost him two places, although he still recovered fourth from Pierre Gasly before the flag. Pierre Gasly - 9/10 An excellent weekend and comfortably Alpine's best result of the season. Reached Q3, stayed with the leading group throughout and was less than three seconds away from victory at the finish. Franco Colapinto - 8.5/10 Another huge result for Alpine. Qualified inside the top 10, stayed out of trouble while plenty around him didn't and converted ninth on the grid into sixth place. Missing Q3 was disappointing and the 10-second time penalty for passing Norris off the circuit was harsh, although being spun by Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc later on was not his fault and he recovered to finish seventh. Carlos Sainz - 8.5/10 A superb recovery from 20th on the grid after his power-unit penalty. top.title: Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable'
top.description: The Ferrari drivers have previously compromised their own races while battling in Italy and Mexico this season [Getty Images] Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Leclerc tipped Hamilton into a spin with 22 laps to go, costing both points in a race where at one stage they were racing with the McLarens, which finished on the podium. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, which meant he finished 10th, three places behind Hamilton, in a race won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen. It was the second race-compromising incident within grands prix, and it came after the drivers had been brought together to clear the air at the last race in Brazil after their first-lap fighting in Mexico cost them a win. Hamilton said such an incident "should never happen" but added that: "The question should be for Ferrari now." Leclerc said: "We just need to fix whatever is not working." Team principal Frederic Vasseur described the situation as "completely unacceptable". Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide The Frenchman said: "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, the same speech as after Mexico. "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake because in this kind of race you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you're passed by others. It means you have to do your race and Charles clearly made a mistake. "It's penalising the team a lot and it's completely unacceptable. Honestly we are more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico, we had a chat together in Brazil, today we passed the message to think about the team when racing together and the outcome is this one." The battle between the two drivers has been tense all season, and in the second part of the year there have been a series of flashpoints, whether it be on-track racing, disputes about how best to work through strategy, and Hamilton ignoring two separate calls to pit in different races, both of which compromised his result, because he was looking at beating Leclerc. Hamilton said: "It's not something I want to really get into." The seven-time champion, who struggled against Leclerc last year but who has been revived in 2026, deflected questions about whether he should be given number-one status. "I've never asked to be number one," he said. "I genuinely haven't ever asked. "There was a point in the season where I was 40-odd points ahead, and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi (Antonelli). "I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year. "At that point, we needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few instances in the season where, with the support, I think we could have beaten Kimi. "But no, that's not what I've asked for. We shouldn't have gotten together. top.title: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe
top.description: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe “Juni Calafat and Jose Angel Sanchez gave me a list of 4-5 strikers to choose from in the summer. I chose Carlos Espi.” These were the words of Jose Mourinho after Real Madrid’s win over Celta Vigo last night, a game in which Carlos Espi came off the bench to score the winner, and not for the first time. The manager heavily praised the new signing for his impact, and understandably so given how he has always found a way to come up clutch for Real Madrid, with his numbers being phenomenal. The best in the world As reported by AS , Espi is the most potent goalscoring substitute in all of Europe, and his efficiency in front of goal is second to none, especially under pressure. Espi’s goals have all led to direct points. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) In just about 73 minutes of football for Real Madrid, he has already scored four goals, all of which came in clutch moments. He averages one goal every 18 minutes. What makes the statistics all the more appalling is that he has scored his four goals from just six shots on target and nine overall shots. His goals have directly helped Real Madrid secure six points in La Liga and two in the UEFA Champions League. Thriving under pressure Espi arrived at Real Madrid knowing full well that Kylian Mbappe would be ahead of him on the pecking order. His role was always going to be one of a substitute, and he has embraced that role with minimal fuss. Espi is thriving under pressure. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Yet, the youngster is seemingly enjoying the responsibility of going out and making a difference in chaotic moments, especially with the clock ticking down. Having the manager’s trust as a player who can make a difference under pressure, after all, is something that can make a player supremely confident. Despite not having regular starts, Espi is thus impressing and making the most of his limited minutes at a range that not many saw coming. It remains to be seen if the manager finds any occasional starting role for Espi, especially given how he blatantly refused the possibility of fielding Mbappe and Espi together. What is for sure, however, is that Real Madrid have a pearl on their hands – one that they would likely not trade for any sum of money.

top.title: Late goals, narrow wins – and back on top
top.description: Late goals, narrow wins – and back on top The win in the Lower Rhine region was no footballing masterclass, but it was further proof of the resilience of Niko Kovac’s team. Gladbach put BVB under pressure with aggressive pressing, particularly in the first half. The Black & Yellows made technical errors, misplaced passes and found few ways to stretch the opposition defence. Although Felix Nmecha had a chance to put them ahead after just five minutes, BVB generally lacked pace and precision. “We weren’t sharp enough in the first half,” admitted the eventual goalscorer. Sporting director Ole Book also noted unnecessary losses of possession that could not be attributed solely to the hosts’ aggressive approach. With patience and, once again, the right substitutions The picture changed after the break. Borussia Dortmund increased the tempo, took more risks and pushed Gladbach increasingly deep into their own half. Once again, Niko Kovac showed a deft touch with his substitutions. Joey Veerman, Mathis Albert and Marcel Sabitzer were all involved in the build-up to the decisive goal. Albert played in Sabitzer, who laid the ball off for Nmecha. The Germany international unleashed a powerful shot from 19 metres to make it 1-0. It was Nmecha’s fifth goal of the season, already a personal best. The timing is also notable: the midfielder has scored three of his five goals in the final 15 minutes. BVB clearly have the patience and the physical reserves to make a decisive impact even in the closing stages. “We’ve scored late goals a lot now because we have the energy to keep playing our game right to the end,” explained goalkeeper Gregor Kobel. In fact, eight of the Black & Yellows’ 17 Bundesliga goals so far have come in the final ten minutes of matches. Almost half their goals have therefore come at a point when other teams are often already running out of energy and concentration. The fact that BVB left it late in Gladbach did not, however, mean the victory was undeserved. After a laboured first half, the Black & Yellows created considerably more chances. They finished with 2.5 expected goals to Gladbach’s 0.7. “Not spectacular, but deserved — in the manner of a top team,” was Book’s apt assessment. top.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has heaped praise on teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett following his match-winning full debut. The 18-year-old inspired Spurs to a 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Saturday, scoring the opener before providing a sublime assist for Dominic Solanke. Academy graduate seizes his Premier League chance Calls for the England Under-19 international to feature had grown louder during a testing 12 months at Spurs, over a year after his senior bow at 16. Following two bright substitute cameos, De Zerbi finalised plans 10 days before Saturday's clash against Ipswich to hand him a maiden top-flight start. Williams-Barnett struck the opener on 15 minutes before embarking on a mazy second-half run to set up Solanke. De Zerbi outlines Maddison plan and defensive demands De Zerbi explained that pairing the teenager closely with James Maddison was key to his freedom, alongside strict instructions issued on Thursday regarding his defensive work rate. "Luca is a special player," De Zerbi said. "I'm not surprised, because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. I think he's lucky, because he's playing in a top club, with top teammates. "I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important. The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. "And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. "And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers. top.title: Expected Goals stats tell the very real story after Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2
top.description: Harvey Barnes Shooting Goal Newcastle v Arsenal Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game. To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing. Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match. With every single shot awarded an xG value based on the difficulty of the attempt, with factors including distance from goal, type of shot and number of defenders present affecting the value. The higher the xG of a particular shot, the more likely a goal should be scored from that shot. The xG value of every shot in a game is then used to calculate the expected goals in a particular match. So rather than just the usual basic statistics of how many shots each team has, Expected Goals factors in where shots were taken from and how good a chance was and whether defenders in the way etc. These Expected Goals stats from Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 Newcastle United 1.73 Arsenal 1.48 As you can see, Newcastle’s Expected Goals stat is higher than Arsenal’s by a decent degree. Not a huge difference but a clear one. When you look at the other stats below, they back up the fact that Newcastle United deserved at the very least a point AND arguably if either side deserved to have won the game, it was United, as they had the better chances overall. As well as the higher Expected Goals stat, Newcastle had twice as many corners (6 v 3), whilst the overall shots (12 v 13) and efforts on target (3 v 4) were almost identical. top.description: Noni Madueke: That wasn’t good enough Despite scoring the goal that rescued a point, Noni Madueke was left frustrated by the way Arsenal allowed control of the game to slip at Newcastle. top.title: Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run
top.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City must tighten up defensively after their winless run continued with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Fulham. City needed an equalizer from Elliot Anderson at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday to avoid a fourth successive Premier League defeat. Anderson’s volley just before the hour mark cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener and, although City were aggrieved that Erling Haaland had a goal disallowed, there was no disguising another disappointing display. City manager Maresca said: “For sure we are conceding too many goals. We need to avoid that. “Sometimes you need to win games 1-0, you need to keep clean sheets and unfortunately, at this moment, we are not able to do that. This is the main thing. “I think we concede almost 80%of our goals in the first 20 minutes, so for sure there is something there that we need to improve. “But I can see many positive aspects and this is something we started four months ago, not four years ago.” The main talking point of the game was referee Thomas Bramall’s decision to chalk off what would have been a leveller from Haaland in the 25th minute. The Norwegian bundled home from close range after Bernd Leno had failed to gather a shot cleanly, but the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. Haaland was perplexed, but the decision was upheld by VAR and the striker then uncharacteristically spurned another good chance soon after. It was left to Anderson to salvage a point for City from what was a largely lacklustre performance. The midfielder marked his return to action after being sent off for England last week when he struck with a low volley from the edge of the area after a corner was cleared. Anderson told the club’s website: “It was a poor first half, unfortunately. We seem to have been going behind recently, but the reaction was really good after half-time. “It just wasn’t enough to get the three points. We had plenty of chances, which seems to be the overall story [lately], but once they start going in, and as maybe we start picking our performances up a little bit more, we’ll be happy.” With Enzo Fernandez on the bench after returning later from international duty, Anderson was deployed in a more advanced role by Maresca. “I played a little bit higher up and got myself a goal,” Anderson said. “I’m just trying to just work on my game. “We tweaked a few things and really went for them, which gave us a bit more control of the game. It’s just unlucky we didn’t get the second.”

nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school. Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the collapse of the building. The deceased, a primary two pupil,was said to have gone to ease himself beside the dilapidated building when the wall suddenly collapsed on him. Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen, said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound. nigeria.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. nigeria.description: The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks. The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy. The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations. The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia. An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a “backwards” step, warning there was a “very real possibility” that COP31 ends with no deal. “I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday,” the official said on condition of anonymity. “The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight,” a German official said. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas. Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise. The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels — but stops short of naming them explicitly. And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. “We are very disappointed with how the text looks,” the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency’s offices. “I can’t honestly say that I’m okay with it passing” in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was “quite silent” on fossil fuels. – Goal to electrify – The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of “clean energy”. The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time. Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card. “Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.” Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow. “The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. sports.title: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe
sports.description: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe “Juni Calafat and Jose Angel Sanchez gave me a list of 4-5 strikers to choose from in the summer. I chose Carlos Espi.” These were the words of Jose Mourinho after Real Madrid’s win over Celta Vigo last night, a game in which Carlos Espi came off the bench to score the winner, and not for the first time. The manager heavily praised the new signing for his impact, and understandably so given how he has always found a way to come up clutch for Real Madrid, with his numbers being phenomenal. The best in the world As reported by AS , Espi is the most potent goalscoring substitute in all of Europe, and his efficiency in front of goal is second to none, especially under pressure. Espi’s goals have all led to direct points. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) In just about 73 minutes of football for Real Madrid, he has already scored four goals, all of which came in clutch moments. He averages one goal every 18 minutes. What makes the statistics all the more appalling is that he has scored his four goals from just six shots on target and nine overall shots. His goals have directly helped Real Madrid secure six points in La Liga and two in the UEFA Champions League. Thriving under pressure Espi arrived at Real Madrid knowing full well that Kylian Mbappe would be ahead of him on the pecking order. Despite not having regular starts, Espi is thus impressing and making the most of his limited minutes at a range that not many saw coming. It remains to be seen if the manager finds any occasional starting role for Espi, especially given how he blatantly refused the possibility of fielding Mbappe and Espi together. What is for sure, however, is that Real Madrid have a pearl on their hands – one that they would likely not trade for any sum of money.

sports.title: Expected Goals stats tell the very real story after Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2
sports.description: Harvey Barnes Shooting Goal Newcastle v Arsenal Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game. To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing. Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match. With every single shot awarded an xG value based on the difficulty of the attempt, with factors including distance from goal, type of shot and number of defenders present affecting the value. The higher the xG of a particular shot, the more likely a goal should be scored from that shot. The xG value of every shot in a game is then used to calculate the expected goals in a particular match. So rather than just the usual basic statistics of how many shots each team has, Expected Goals factors in where shots were taken from and how good a chance was and whether defenders in the way etc. These Expected Goals stats from Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 Newcastle United 1.73 Arsenal 1.48 As you can see, Newcastle’s Expected Goals stat is higher than Arsenal’s by a decent degree. Not a huge difference but a clear one. When you look at the other stats below, they back up the fact that Newcastle United deserved at the very least a point AND arguably if either side deserved to have won the game, it was United, as they had the better chances overall. As well as the higher Expected Goals stat, Newcastle had twice as many corners (6 v 3), whilst the overall shots (12 v 13) and efforts on target (3 v 4) were almost identical. sports.title: Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run
sports.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City must tighten up defensively after their winless run continued with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Fulham. City needed an equalizer from Elliot Anderson at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday to avoid a fourth successive Premier League defeat. Anderson’s volley just before the hour mark cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener and, although City were aggrieved that Erling Haaland had a goal disallowed, there was no disguising another disappointing display. City manager Maresca said: “For sure we are conceding too many goals. We need to avoid that. “Sometimes you need to win games 1-0, you need to keep clean sheets and unfortunately, at this moment, we are not able to do that. This is the main thing. “I think we concede almost 80%of our goals in the first 20 minutes, so for sure there is something there that we need to improve. “But I can see many positive aspects and this is something we started four months ago, not four years ago.” The main talking point of the game was referee Thomas Bramall’s decision to chalk off what would have been a leveller from Haaland in the 25th minute. The Norwegian bundled home from close range after Bernd Leno had failed to gather a shot cleanly, but the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. Haaland was perplexed, but the decision was upheld by VAR and the striker then uncharacteristically spurned another good chance soon after. It was left to Anderson to salvage a point for City from what was a largely lacklustre performance. The midfielder marked his return to action after being sent off for England last week when he struck with a low volley from the edge of the area after a corner was cleared. Anderson told the club’s website: “It was a poor first half, unfortunately. We seem to have been going behind recently, but the reaction was really good after half-time. “It just wasn’t enough to get the three points. We had plenty of chances, which seems to be the overall story [lately], but once they start going in, and as maybe we start picking our performances up a little bit more, we’ll be happy.” With Enzo Fernandez on the bench after returning later from international duty, Anderson was deployed in a more advanced role by Maresca. “I played a little bit higher up and got myself a goal,” Anderson said. “I’m just trying to just work on my game. “We tweaked a few things and really went for them, which gave us a bit more control of the game. It’s just unlucky we didn’t get the second.”

sports.title: Max Verstappen labels George Russell a ‘joke’ and ‘so far below my level’ in stinging remarks
sports.description: Max Verstappen declared that George Russell was “so far below my level” in a series of stinging remarks about his Formula 1 rival after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix . The duo, who clashed in a series of heated confrontations on track and in the media at the end of the 2024 season, have reignited their rivalry this weekend in Las Vegas after an incident in final practice on Saturday. Russell stated that Verstappen “screwed him over” after the pair collided, adding that the Dutchman believes he is “bigger and better than everyone else.” The pair started on the front row and astonishingly traded places with Russell 12 times during a breathless race in Sin City. Yet with a handful of laps remaining, Russell misjudged an overtake on teammate Kimi Antonelli and hit the barrier. Verstappen stormed to victory while the Briton finished down in ninth. "Ha ha, well done! My God," laughed Verstappen on team radio when the incident occurred. Then, in an interview with Dutch broadcaster ViaPlay, Verstappen took aim at Russell. "This actually had nothing to do with Formula 1," he said "But I did enjoy some of the action. Especially because one person in particular didn't stand a chance. He [Russell] deserves that too. “His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me. All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect Karma." Speaking later in the FIA press conference, Verstappen elaborated: "It doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. "So it doesn't bother me. And today, Karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. "I was like, 'Fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete." Verstappen and Russell also clashed last year after the Dutchman deliberately rammed the Mercedes driver at the Spanish Grand Prix in Barcelona. In a season where the majority had Russell as the pre-season favourite, his Mercedes teammate Antonelli has romped to the world championship while second-placed Verstappen is now 40 points clear of Russell with two rounds remaining. The next round is the Qatar Grand Prix on 29 November.

sports.description: FC Bayern have made headlines this past week as the club’s management has opened a wildly insensitive public dialogue about Jamal Musiala’s health and contract with the club. Many have rushed to critici ze this approach, and club legend Lothar Matthäus is the next to join the list. Speaking to Sky Sport after Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln, Matthäus delivered a scathing critique of the various statements made by those in charge at Bayern. “I’ve actually been a bit shocked throughout this entire week. It started with Uli Hoeneß, continued with Jan-Christian Dreesen, and yesterday Kar l-Heinz Rummenigge chose the strongest words of all. I have enormous respect for Karl-He inz. sports.description: Barcelona face fresh hurdle in pursuit of key target as his club demand more than €20m – report According to SPORT , Barcelona have stepped up their efforts to sign Ruud Nijstad from FC Twente ahead of the January transfer window, but the Dutch club are making an agreement difficult. The 18-year-old centre-back has become one of the Catalan giants’ preferred defensive targets , but any move for the youngster will be complicated due to Twente’s demands. Nijstad open to Barcelona move Having already tried to sign Nijstad in the summer, Barcelona have renewed contact with Twente in an attempt to revive the operation in the January transfer window. Nijstad was initially inclined to continue his development in the Netherlands, but his position has softened after learning more about the sporting project being offered by the La Liga champions. The 18-year-old starlet is particularly attracted by Barcelona’s willingness to give opportunities to emerging players. As such, he sees the Blaugrana as the ideal environment to continue his development, making a move to Camp Nou increasingly appealing. Barcelona want Nijstad in January. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB) While this is an encouraging development as far as Barcelona are concerned, convincing the player is only part of the challenge. Twente demand more than €20 million Indeed, as per the report, Twente’s financial demands are making the transfer increasingly complicated. The Dutch club have raised their asking price and are now demanding more than €20 million to sanction his departure. A left-footed centre-back with an impressive ability to play out from the back, Barça see the teenager as a good fit into their tactical setup. However, Barcelona consider that figure excessive for an 18-year-old who still has relatively limited experience at the highest level. Although the Catalans are convinced by Nijstad’s potential, they are reluctant to commit such a substantial amount to a player whose development is far from complete. Barcelona do not want to spend big on Nijstad. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Moreover, Twente want to retain Nijstad until the end of the current campaign, even if they agree to sell him during the January window. The Dutch club would consider negotiating a permanent transfer in January on the condition that the teenage defender returns to them on loan until June. For Barcelona, however, the idea does not fit with their intention to bring Nijstad in during the winter window, making the possibility of a deal extremely difficult. Beyond these two complications, Barcelona also have to deal with the fact hat the youngster is attracting interest from the Premier League. Chelsea, Manchester City and Manchester United are all monitoring Nijstad’s development, and their interest could make an already difficult negotiation even more complex.

sports.title: 'We're underdogs': New MI coach makes honest admission ahead of IPL 2027 season
sports.description: 'We're underdogs': New MI coach makes honest admission ahead of IPL 2027 season originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Robin Uthappa has been appointed Mumbai Indians ' batting coach ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He says the five-time champions feel like underdogs and must earn back supporters' trust. Mumbai finished ninth in 2026 and have gone six seasons without a title. Robin Uthappa says Mumbai Indians feel like underdogs going into IPL 2027 Five titles usually buy a franchise some patience, but Mumbai Indians have not won one since 2020 and finished ninth last season with four wins from 14 matches. Their new batting coach is not pretending otherwise. Robin Uthappa, who took the job as part of a wholesale change to the coaching staff, framed the coming season in terms most people associate with a struggling side rather than the most decorated in the competition. "As Mumbai Indians, we feel like we're underdogs," he said in an interaction with select media, reported by NDTV . He went further on what the squad owes the people who follow it. "We really need to earn our stripes back and earn the trust of the fans. There are a lot of things that we have to work towards as a team," Uthappa added. The appointment itself caught him off guard. "It completely came from left field. I didn't see it coming," said the two-time IPL winner, who is currently commentating at the DP World ILT20 in the UAE, adding that he had been hoping for a call from the franchise because he believed he could add value to it. MORE: MI likely auction targets: Who will they buy in IPL 2027 mini-auction? What Mumbai Indians have changed after six seasons without an IPL title Uthappa is one piece of an overhaul that has touched almost every part of the setup. Kieron Pollard, who held the batting role last season, has been elevated to head coach, former India fielding coach T Dilip takes the fielding brief, and Mitchell McClenaghan returns to the franchise as bowling coach. The playing side has moved just as far. Hardik Pandya, who captained through the ninth-place finish, has gone to Punjab Kings in the trade that brought Arshdeep Singh the other way, and Mumbai have changed captain for 2027, with Rohit Sharma widely reported to be taking the job back. Uthappa's answer to all of it was to talk about humility rather than personnel. "Nobody is bigger than Mother Cricket. We've all been in the game long enough to know that nobody can beat Mother Cricket. You have to operate from that humility," he said. He described his own role as a supporting one rather than a corrective one. "I'm only a mirror to them, holding them accountable for what they want to achieve and aligning that with the larger goal of the team," Uthappa said. sports.title: Hawks Hits: Rinzel Makes History, Fighting Through Adversity, Frondell Injured
sports.description: Nearly two full months into the season, the Chicago Blackhawks finally earned their first road win in 10 tries on Saturday night, defeating the Calgary Flames 4-3 in overtime at Scotiabank Saddledome. The Blackhawks were the only NHL team still without a road win entering Saturday, and they had to overcome plenty of adversity to change that in Calgary. The countless hardships and seemingly never-ending misfortune in the first quarter of this season are starting to harden the young Hawks group. Already without captain Connor Bedard in the lineup for the second straight game due to his latest shoulder injury , the Blackhawks also lost defenseman Wyatt Kaiser and center Anton Frondell on Saturday, leaving only 16 skaters for the third period and overtime. With a shortened visiting bench, and the Flames carrying all the momentum late after clawing back from a 3-1 deficit, the Blackhawks dug deep to push the game to 3-on-3 play. Then, after Frank Nazar drew a penalty with a tremendous solo effort, the power play converted just after Yegor Sharangovich stepped out of the penalty box, with Sam Rinzel fittingly responsible for the game-winner. “I thought our guys, with the loss of Frondell and Kaiser, we had to gut it out. Especially after giving up the early goal in the third [period]. It wasn’t necessarily our best third, but we found a way to bend not break.” Another obstacle the Hawks faced was an overturned overtime-winner from Roman Kantserov , who became the first NHL rookie to reach 10 goals this season earlier in the game. Kantserov’s net-front tap-in from Patrick Kane ‘s pass was reversed for a careless offside by Nazar, setting the stage for another potential disastrous loss that would have perfectly described the tumultuous season thus far. But despite all the bumps in the road, the Blackhawks stuck with it and found a second game-winning goal in overtime, with no dispute from the Flames or video review necessary for Rinzel’s tally. Since the disastrous three-game Southeastern road trip and GM Kyle Davidson’s state-of-the-union press conference, the Blackhawks have done well to smooth the waters around a rocking ship. They’re now 3-1-1 in the last five games, and all three wins have been character-builders. Their win over the Buffalo Sabres on Nov. 12 marked the first time they earned two points when trailing entering the third period this season. That victory was particularly needed, considering it was the Hawks’ first game after an embarrassing 9-2 loss in Carolina. Then, when Bedard got injured in Tuesday’s game against the Toronto Maple Leafs, the Blackhawks didn’t let it take the wind out of their sails and sealed the win for their captain, scoring a season-high six goals. Now, the Blackhawks have won away from the United Center for the first time this year, which should give the group added confidence that they can do it again on Sunday in Vancouver. sports.title: 'Right now Malen is extraordinary!' - Gian Piero Gasperini explains how former Aston Villa striker matched a 66-year Roma record with four-goal Parma demolition
sports.description: FBL-ITA-SERIE A-PARMA-ROMA - AFP Donyell Malen netted four goals in Roma's 5-1 Serie A demolition of Parma to equal an all-time club record for calendar-year league strikes. Coach Gian Piero Gasperini hailed the former Aston Villa forward as "extraordinary" after his 26th Serie A goal of 2026 kept the Giallorossi within two points of leaders Lazio. Malen hits four to equal 66-year Roma record Donyell Malen scored four times to inspire Roma to an emphatic 5-1 Serie A victory over Parma and keep Gian Piero Gasperini's side just two points behind league leaders Lazio. Rodrigo Mora added Roma's other goal after Nesta Elphege had briefly equalised on the counter-attack for the hosts. The four-goal haul took Malen to 12 goals in the opening 12 league rounds and 26 Serie A strikes across the 2026 calendar year since arriving from Aston Villa in January. That tally draws the Netherlands international level with Pedro Manfredini's all-time club record set in 1960, with more than a month of the year still remaining. Gasperini explains why Malen thrives in his system Speaking to DAZN Italia after the final whistle, Gasperini praised his team's response to conceding an equaliser and singled out Malen's tactical compatibility with Roma's attacking style. "Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, you don't play at that level without quality," Gasperini said. "Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way. There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents, and of course Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary. He combines so well with our team, we perhaps get more out of Malen than we would do with a striker who is stronger on paper, but doesn't fit as well with our style of football." From Villa loanee to record-breaking talisman Malen initially joined Roma on loan from Aston Villa on 16 January 2026 before completing a permanent €25 million move in May on a contract running until June 2030 after firing the club back into the UEFA Champions League. His latest four-goal outing also marked his third Serie A hat-trick of 2026—a feat last achieved in the Italian top flight by Josip Ilicic, who also played under Gasperini at Atalanta. Roma's 36 goals across their first 12 league fixtures represent the highest total by any Serie A team in 76 years, since Inter, Milan and Juventus all surpassed that mark in the 1950-51 season. Title race momentum builds with fixtures left in 2026 With Roma sitting on 30 points and chasing Lazio at the summit, Gasperini noted that overcoming adversity at Parma showed his squad's growing belief. For Malen, standing level with Manfredini on 26 calendar-year league goals in late November leaves ample opportunity to claim the all-time Roma record outright before 2026 concludes.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor.

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998: Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos) Why it mattered As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet. The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue."
